cohort: The study included 13,221 families with term singletons from the Taiwan Birth Cohort Study, whose mothers gave birth in 2005.
finding: Both mother's and father's shift work before pregnancy were associated with an increased risk of adverse pregnancy outcomes, with father's shift work particularly linked to excessive GWG among mothers not doing shift work.
mod_finding: Parental shift work before pregnancy was associated with higher odds of Caesarean section.
